correctness.rationale: The regular differential witness has pole weight p^(t-1)(q^n-q+1)-q^2 <= 2g-2. In the explicit Cartier rule its y-positive chain has t-1 unit transitions, then maps to -x^(p^(t(n-1)-1)-1) dx, and t(n-1)-1 further Cartier steps yield -dx. Thus C^(tn-1) is nonzero. Garcia--Tafazolian 2008 Theorem 3.3 plus maximality of X(q,n) over F_(q^(2n)) proves C^(tn)=0. A standalone exact arithmetic checker verifies twelve finite cases; finite verification is not substituted for the proof.
